Vulnerability assessment & CVE vulnerability mapping
Web application security (OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities)
Reconnaissance techniques (Passive & Active discovery)
Penetration testing execution frameworks
Controlled attack simulations & privilege escalation
Security monitoring & perimeter telemetry analysis
SIEM configuration & log analysis (Splunk, Elastic)
Threat detection rules (YARA, Sigma)
Incident response triage & forensic stabilization

Disk forensics & RAW / E01 filesystem image carving
Network forensics & deep protocol trace inspection
Incident investigation & post-breach reconstruction

Log correlation & timeline triage synthesis

domains.name: Cryptography
domains.tagline: The mathematics that allows two parties to establish trust across an untrusted wire — turning plaintext into ciphertext impenetrable to adversaries.
domains.overview: Cryptography forms the foundational mathematical backbone of all digital trust. Members explore symmetric and asymmetric encryption primitives, cryptographic hashing, digital signatures, public key infrastructure (PKI), and zero-knowledge proof concepts.
focusAreas: Encryption & decryption mathematics and modular arithmetic
Asymmetric cryptography (RSA, Elliptic Curve Cryptography)
Digital signatures, certificates, and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)
Symmetric ciphers (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305)
Cryptographic hashing (SHA-2, SHA-3, BLAKE3, collision resistance)
Key management, exchange protocols (Diffie-Hellman), and HSM architectures
Cryptanalysis, padding oracle attacks, and side-channel vulnerabilities

awarenessArticles.summary: Following more than two decades of collaborative open-source engineering, real-time Linux support (PREEMPT_RT) has been officially integrated into the mainline Linux kernel 6.12, providing deterministic latency for robotics and mission-critical systems.

awarenessArticles.summary: The Python Software Foundation has officially released Python 3.13 featuring an experimental build that disables the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), enabling multi-threaded Python code to run in true multi-core parallel execution.

awarenessArticles.summary: A critical vulnerability with CVSS 9.8 in Apache Tomcat allows unauthenticated remote adversaries to execute arbitrary JSP code on case-insensitive filesystems due to a race condition between concurrent upload requests.

awarenessArticles.title: CERT-In Issues High Severity Advisory for Critical Vulnerabilities in Google Chrome and Android
awarenessArticles.summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) published advisory CIVN-2025-0012 warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Google Chrome and Android that could allow remote adversaries to execute code and access system memory.

awarenessArticles.title: CISA and FBI Issue Joint Advisory on Salt Typhoon Telecom Cyber Espionage Operations
awarenessArticles.summary: U.S. cybersecurity agencies confirmed threat group Salt Typhoon compromised commercial telecommunications providers, gaining unauthorized access to customer call record metadata and lawful interception systems.

awarenessArticles.title: CISA Adds Actively Exploited Palo Alto Networks Expedition Flaws to KEV Catalog
awarenessArticles.summary: CISA added CVE-2024-5910 and CVE-2024-5911 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmed active exploitation allowing attackers to reset administrative credentials on firewall migration systems.

awarenessArticles.title: Part-Time "Task & YouTube Like" Scam Targeting University Students
awarenessArticles.summary: Fraudsters lure students through unsolicited WhatsApp and Telegram messages promising high daily payouts for simple video-liking tasks, then coerce them into transferring large deposits for "prepaid tasks".
awarenessArticles.source: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal Analysis
howItWorks: Victim receives an unsolicited WhatsApp or Telegram message offering ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per day for liking YouTube videos or leaving 5-star Google reviews.
Scammers pay initial small amounts (₹150 to ₹500) via UPI to build trust and prove legitimacy.
Victim is added to a private Telegram channel displaying fake payment receipts and members celebrating profits.
Scammers introduce "Prepaid Merchant Tasks" requiring the student to deposit ₹5,000 to ₹50,000 to unlock higher commission balances.
When the victim attempts to withdraw funds, fraudsters demand additional "tax clearance" or "system unlock" fees until the victim realizes they have been defrauded.
redFlags: Unsolicited job offers received via WhatsApp or Telegram without prior application.
Guaranteed high daily earnings for trivial online actions.
Any requirement to pay money or deposit security funds in order to receive your earned salary.
Recruiters operating exclusively through Telegram channels rather than verified corporate email domains.
safetyTips: Never deposit money to secure employment, interviews, or release earned commissions.
Verify recruiter credentials on official corporate career portals or through college placement cells.
Block and report phone numbers and Telegram groups offering unverified work-from-home tasks.
Warn classmates and roommates about task schemes operating across campus social networks.
awarenessArticles.whatToDoIfTargeted: Cease all communication immediately. Do not transfer further money to "unfreeze" your funds. Preserve chat screenshots, phone numbers, and UPI transaction reference numbers. Immediately call the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 and register a formal complaint on cybercrime.gov.in.

awarenessArticles.title: UPI "Scan QR Code to Receive Money" Reverse Pay Fraud
awarenessArticles.summary: Scammers posing as buyers on marketplace apps send a QR code claiming it will deposit money into the seller's account, tricking victims into entering their UPI PIN and authorizing an outgoing transfer.
howItWorks: Scammer contacts a student or seller on OLX, Quickr, or social marketplace agreeing to purchase an item without haggling.
Scammer claims they can only transfer funds via UPI and sends a QR code image over chat.
Scammer falsely insists: "Scan this QR code and enter your 4-digit or 6-digit UPI PIN to claim your payment into your bank account."
The moment the victim scans the QR and enters their PIN, the payment app debits money from the victim's bank account instead of crediting it.
redFlags: Any instruction to enter your UPI PIN to receive money — UPI PIN is strictly for DEBITING funds.
Buyer demands an immediate transaction via custom QR code rather than using standard bank transfer.
Deceptive text overlays on QR images saying "Scan to Receive Payment".
safetyTips: Golden Rule: You NEVER need to enter your UPI PIN to receive money into your bank account.
Never scan a QR code sent by a third party claiming it will deposit funds into your wallet.
Only provide your UPI ID (VPA) or registered phone number to receive payments safely.
awarenessArticles.whatToDoIfTargeted: Immediately block your UPI ID and payment app. Call your bank's 24x7 fraud hotline within the "golden hour" to request a transaction freeze. Dial 1930 to notify cyber police.

awarenessArticles.title: "Digital Arrest" & Fake Law Enforcement Video Call Scheme
awarenessArticles.summary: Sophisticated criminal syndicates impersonate Police, CBI, or Customs officers over Skype or WhatsApp video calls, alleging illegal contraband was intercepted in the victim's name and demanding money transfers under threat of immediate arrest.
howItWorks: Victim receives an automated IVR call stating their parcel containing passports, narcotics, or illegal goods has been seized by Customs at Mumbai or Delhi airport.
Call is transferred to a fraudster impersonating a police or CBI investigator wearing uniforms against a staged police station backdrop on Skype.
Scammers claim the victim's Aadhaar is linked to money laundering and place them under "Digital Arrest", ordering them not to leave their room.
Victim is threatened with prosecution unless they transfer their bank savings to a "Supreme Court Verification Account" for security clearance.
redFlags: There is NO provision for "Digital Arrest" under Indian criminal law or police procedure.
Police or investigative agencies NEVER conduct interrogation or arrest citizens over Skype or WhatsApp video calls.
No legitimate government agency will EVER ask you to transfer personal funds to a bank account for verification.
safetyTips: Disconnect the call immediately if anyone mentions "digital arrest" or threatens arrest via phone or video.
Do not share your Aadhaar number, banking details, or OTPs with unknown callers.
Report fraudulent caller numbers on the Department of Telecommunications Chakshu portal.
awarenessArticles.whatToDoIfTargeted: Hang up immediately. Do not transfer funds. Report the incident to 1930 and file a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in. Report the phone number on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu).

awarenessArticles.title: Fake Campus Placement & Job Portal Spoofing
awarenessArticles.summary: Scammers send counterfeit recruitment letters mimicking top tier IT companies demanding ₹1,500 to ₹3,500 "document verification and gate pass fees" before campus interview dates.
howItWorks: Students receive emails displaying corporate logos offering direct interview slots or provisional offer letters.
Email demands payment of a "refundable training kit fee" or "background verification charge" via UPI within 24 hours.
Once payment is completed, candidate receives fake receipts and the scammers' communication lines go dead.
redFlags: Emails originating from free webmail accounts like @gmail.com or @outlook.com claiming to represent major IT employers.
Any fee requirement for interviews, test scheduling, or offer letter issuance.
Grammatical mistakes, mismatched sender domains, or urgent payment deadlines.
safetyTips: Top technology firms (TCS, Infosys, Cognizant, Wipro, Accenture) NEVER charge candidate recruitment fees.
Cross-check all placement drives directly with the college Training & Placement Cell (T&P).
Inspect the sender's full email address and headers before opening attachments.
awarenessArticles.whatToDoIfTargeted: Alert your college Placement Officer and Department Head immediately to protect fellow classmates. File an incident report on cybercrime.gov.in with transaction details.

awarenessArticles.title: AI Voice Cloning & Family Emergency Extortion
awarenessArticles.summary: Cybercriminals harvest audio snippets from social media reels and videos to clone a student's voice using AI, calling parents in distress to demand immediate ransom or medical fee transfers.
howItWorks: Scammers scrape short audio clips of a student from public Instagram reels, YouTube videos, or podcasts.
Generative AI voice models clone the student's exact pitch, cadence, and vocal quirks.
Scammers place an urgent call to the parents, playing the cloned voice crying for help after a fabricated car accident or police detention.
An accomplice demands an immediate UPI transfer of ₹50,000 to settle the hospital or police matter, warning not to hang up.
redFlags: Intense emotional pressure, panic, and demand for immediate funds transfer.
Caller refuses to let you hang up or contact the student's personal phone number.
Payment requested through personal UPI IDs rather than hospital or institutional bank accounts.
safetyTips: Establish a confidential "Family Safe Word" known only to close family members to verify authentic distress.
Always pause and call the student directly on their regular phone number or call their college roommate or hostel warden.
Keep personal social media accounts private to limit public voice harvesting.
awarenessArticles.whatToDoIfTargeted: Disconnect the call immediately and call the student directly. If funds were transferred, immediately call 1930 and report to the local police cyber cell.
